original_question: For the same real analytic single-input time-optimal control setting, can one always choose a time-optimal trajectory between two time-optimally connected points whose set of switching points avoids having positive measure?
target_in_paper: Section I.B, the unnumbered open problem in the real-analytic single-input time-optimal setting, specifically the weaker page-2 question immediately following the main countability question: "We do not know if we can avoid a positive measure set of switching points."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right subsection of the paper: the real-analytic, single-input, fixed-endpoint time-optimal control problem, with the existential quantifier taken over all time-optimal trajectories joining the same two endpoints. It also correctly focuses on the weaker subsidiary open issue from that subsection—whether one can choose an optimal trajectory whose switching set is not too large—rather than on generic smooth systems.
missing_details: The paper’s control system should be stated explicitly: q̇ = f(q) + u g(q), with scalar control u satisfying |u| ≤ 1.
The ambient space is a real analytic n-dimensional manifold M, and the vector fields f and g are real analytic.
The vector fields are not assumed generic in Section I.B; that non-genericity is part of the intended scope.
Admissible controls are measurable functions, and admissible trajectories are Lipschitz curves.
The paper phrases the endpoint hypothesis as: two points are connected by at least one time-optimal trajectory.
A switching point is defined earlier in Section I as a point where the admissible trajectory is not smooth.
The open content is only nontrivial in dimensions n ≥ 3, since for n = 2 the paper recalls a stronger positive result: one can choose a time-optimal trajectory with finitely many switching points.
The paper presents your target question as a weaker subsidiary issue that follows the stronger main open question asking for an optimal trajectory with at most countably many switching points.
To make the question fully stand-alone, the meaning of 'positive measure' should be tied to the 1-dimensional parameter set of switching points/times along the trajectory.
refined_question: Let M be a real analytic n-dimensional manifold, and let f and g be real analytic vector fields on M, not assumed generic. Consider the fixed-endpoint time-optimal problem for the single-input control-affine system q̇ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| ≤ 1, with measurable controls u and Lipschitz admissible trajectories. Assume that two points q0, q1 ∈ M are connected by at least one time-optimal trajectory. In the nontrivial case n ≥ 3, must there exist a time-optimal trajectory from q0 to q1 whose set of switching points—i.e. points where the trajectory is not smooth—does not have positive measure?
justification: The draft is aimed at Section I.B, not at the generic C∞ problem in Section I.A. In Section I.B the paper first fixes the real-analytic control-affine system and explains that, although arbitrary optimal trajectories may be very irregular, one hopes that among all time-optimal trajectories with the same endpoints there is at least one with better switching behavior. After recalling that finite switching is known in dimension 2 but fails already in dimension 3 via the Fuller phenomenon, the paper states a stronger main open question about countably many switching points and then immediately records the weaker unresolved issue that matches your draft: whether one can avoid a positive-measure set of switching points. The refined question therefore keeps your weaker target, but adds the precise system, admissibility, analyticity, endpoint quantifier, non-generic scope, and the dimension context needed to make it faithful and stand-alone.
